solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Like a cat, black and suffering from fleas?

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
flea bites leave you itchy

explanation.surface: A description of a dark, flea-ridden moggy scratching itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like a cat' looks like the cat itself, but it is the sense 'catty': spiteful.
explanation.definitionFit: Catty and bitchy are both synonyms for spitefully malicious in speech.

clue.text: Refuses to touch vessel in dangerous position

parts.note: trade unions black goods or firms, refusing to handle them
a pot is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: Someone shuns a ship lying in a hazardous spot.
explanation.walkthrough: To black something is British trade-union usage for boycotting it.
explanation.definitionFit: A black spot is a place where accidents often happen, so it is a hazardous location.

clue.text: Writer's counterpart receiving top mark

definitions.note: the definition is Writer, with the 's read as is

indicators.note: receiving means the counterpart takes the grade letter inside it

parts.note: a twin is an exact counterpart
A is the top grade in marking

explanation.surface: A writer's double gets the highest grade.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Twain was the pen name of Samuel Clemens; 'top mark' may hint at that Mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain, author of Tom Sawyer, is a famous American novelist.

clue.text: Don't you get married, shortly husband will be up for something sticky

indicators.note: will be up, in a down entry, means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to wed is to get married
ye is the old form of you
no as a refusal, don't
H is the short form of husband

explanation.surface: A plea not to marry, as the husband will soon be up for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be up' reverses WEDYENOH to give the answer, so each piece reads backwards: ON, EY, DEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeydew is the sugary secretion left on leaves by aphids, a sticky substance.

clue.text: Energy drink first, then grub cooked for one not responding to treatment

indicators.note: first says the drink comes ahead of the energy letter in the answer

parts.note: to sup is to drink, in small mouthfuls
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: cooked suggests the word grub is doctored into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe: energy drink first, then some grub cooked, for one person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy drink' reads as one item, a can of pop, but it splits in two, and 'first' swaps their order. 'cooked' rearranges the grub.
explanation.definitionFit: A superbug is a bacterium resistant to antibiotics, so infections it causes do not respond to treatment.

clue.text: In the way as very young son announced achievement

parts.note: under one year old means very young

indicators.note: announced means the word for achievement is heard said

parts.note: a feat is an achievement

explanation.surface: A very young son's achievement is proudly announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announced' turns FEAT into its sound-alike FEET.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone under one's feet is a nuisance always getting in one's way, an idiom.

clue.text: Speech extolling a group we've left?

definitions.text: Speech extolling a group we've left?

parts.words: Speech extolling a group we've left?
parts.note: a tribute speech to the departed reads here as praise of the European Union, which Britain left

explanation.walkthrough: The answer begins EU; a funeral tribute is spoken for those who have left us.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a speech praising someone, usually at a funeral, an oration of praise.

clue.text: Halt decline: get this to moon

definitions.meaning: to moon is to show one's bare backside

explanation.walkthrough: 'moon' looks like the place stocks go 'to the moon'; it is the prank of baring one's behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Markets bottom out at their lowest level before recovering, and mooning puts the bottom out.

clue.text: A convolution of brain surgery ordered without hesitation

indicators.note: ordered says the remaining letters are arranged anew
without means the hesitation sound is removed

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Brain surgery is prescribed to go ahead without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops ER from SURGERY to leave SURGY, which 'ordered' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A gyrus is one of the ridges on the brain's surface, a fold or convolution of the cortex.

clue.text: Opposing military commander isn't bad

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander or chief

indicators.note: bad indicates the letters of isn't are spoilt into another order

explanation.surface: A judgement that an opposing army's general is not a bad sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' turns ISNT into INST. AGA is a crossword regular for an Ottoman officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be against something is to be opposed to it; the words are synonyms as prepositions or adjectives.

clue.text: Sort of explosion shattered column in the back

indicators.note: in places the scrambled column inside the phrase for the back

parts.note: the rear means the back

indicators.note: shattered says the letters of column are broken up

explanation.surface: A blast shatters a pillar at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the broken-up column (shattered) inside THE REAR, which is 'the back' as a phrase, not just REAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermonuclear explosion comes from nuclear fusion, as in a hydrogen bomb, a type of blast.

clue.text: Stretcher brought when fashion designer clutches muscle

indicators.note: clutches means the designer's name holds the muscle inside it

parts.note: Christian Dior was a French fashion designer
LAT is short for latissimus dorsi, a back muscle

explanation.surface: A stretcher is carried in while a couturier grips a strong man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretcher' suggests a hospital trolley; here it is something that stretches.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilator is an instrument or muscle that widens an opening, so it literally stretches things.

clue.text: Eccentric family okay occasionally

parts.note: kin means one's family or relatives

indicators.note: occasionally asks for only some letters of okay, every other one

explanation.surface: An odd family that is all right now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the second and fourth letters of OKAY, giving KY.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinky can mean quirky or unusual, a looser synonym for odd behaviour or taste.

clue.text: Say nothing a sort of professor holds outrageous

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg

indicators.note: holds means the professor's title has the zero letter inside it

parts.note: a Regius professor holds a chair founded by the Crown at a British university
O, the shape of zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Keep quiet when a certain professor is behaving scandalously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say nothing' reads as one instruction to keep mum; split it into EG and O. A Regius professorship is a royal-founded chair at old British universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Egregious means shockingly bad, a close synonym of outrageous.

clue.text: On page record name in passport for sucker

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: in places the name letter within the word for a pass

parts.note: a permit is a document granting passage, like a passport

explanation.surface: Instructions for noting a name on the page of a passport, for some dupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sucker' suggests a gullible person; it means a sweet one sucks.
explanation.definitionFit: A peppermint is a mint sweet that is sucked, so it is a sucker in the confectionery sense.

clue.text: I introduce quietly aggrieved person

definitions.note: the clue speaks as the answer: a host who says 'I introduce', so a noun

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
a resenter feels aggrieved

explanation.surface: Someone quietly introduces themselves as a person with a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer speaking for itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A presenter is the host of a broadcast, whose job is introducing guests and items.

clue.text: Low river in high ground

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A contrast between a low-lying river and the uplands it passes through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like the opposite of high, but it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A moor is an open upland tract of uncultivated land, so it is high ground.

clue.text: Get back up from police in cup-tie

indicators.note: in means the officers sit inside the match

parts.note: a drawn cup-tie in British football goes to a replay
DIs are detective inspectors, police officers

explanation.surface: Getting back up after police are drafted in at a football cup match.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup-tie is a knockout football match; draws were settled by a replay.
explanation.definitionFit: To redisplay is to put back on show, to get something back up on view.

clue.text: Separate set cried to be put together

indicators.note: to be put together means these letters are assembled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A set cried out to be reunited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be put together' looks like the opposite of the definition, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means distinct and individual, separate from others.

clue.text: Get together in turn and be in large numbers

indicators.note: in turn says the word for gathering is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: to meet is to get together

explanation.surface: People gather one after another and so turn up in crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: To teem is to be present in great quantity, or swarm, as in streets teeming with people.

clue.text: Girl's relative almost died alone

parts.note: Una is a girl's name; with the 's it gives UNAS

indicators.note: almost means the relative's name loses its final letter

parts.note: a sister is a family relative
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A sad story: a girl's relative very nearly died on her own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SISTER to SISTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unassisted means without help from anyone, so you do it alone.

clue.text: Old people as outspoken investigators

indicators.note: outspoken means as is heard spoken aloud

parts.note: the word as is spoken with a buzzing sound, like the letters AZ
tecs is slang for detectives

explanation.surface: Elderly folk act as frank detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outspoken' applies to 'as', heard as AZ.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs were the people of the ancient Mexican empire, an old civilisation.

clue.text: Final character in set troubled revolutionary philosopher

indicators.note: troubled indicates these letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: Z is the final character of the alphabet
Che Guevara was a Marxist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A disturbed revolutionary philosopher, shown as the last word in a troubled set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' shuffles Z with IN and SET to give NIETZS; 'in' is fodder, not an insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Nietzsche was a nineteenth-century German thinker, an example of a philosopher.

clue.text: Moved slowly in Lourdes, only standing up a little

indicators.note: standing up says the hidden letters are read backwards
a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pilgrim inching along at Lourdes, able to stand only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up', in a down entry, reverses DESON.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose is to edge forward cautiously, as a car noses into traffic.

clue.text: Smacks on the wrist?

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means strikes with the open hand
the ends of sleeves at the wrist, or handcuffs

explanation.walkthrough: 'a smack on the wrist' is a mild reprimand; the clue splits that phrase into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuff is a light blow, and the cuff of a sleeve sits on the wrist.

clue.text: Waste silk, following damage

parts.note: loss can mean damage or harm suffered

explanation.surface: Silk goes to waste after some damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Floss is the rough silk from the outside of a silkworm's cocoon, unusable waste silk.

clue.text: Sneering expression at this point on drunk

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the second piece after the first

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
here means at this point or place

explanation.surface: A drunk sneers at someone at this point in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: 'So there!' is a taunting exclamation used to triumph over someone, a sneer in words.

clue.text: Sort of knot judge has to work round

indicators.note: round means the word for labour goes around the official

parts.note: toil means hard work
a ref, or referee, judges a game

explanation.surface: A judge is required to work around a tricky knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'judge' is the sporting referee, REF.
explanation.definitionFit: The trefoil knot is the simplest true knot in mathematics, a three-lobed type of knot.

clue.text: Ridiculous day your old dad returned

indicators.note: returned means the following words come back in reverse order

parts.note: yr is the abbreviated form of your
a sire is a father, a dad

explanation.surface: Your old dad came back on a laughable day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns YROSIRE into ERISORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Derisory means so small or inadequate as to be laughable, a synonym of ridiculous.

clue.text: Inferior male one avoids without trouble

indicators.note: avoids means the word for one stays out of the adverb

parts.note: easily means without trouble
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An inferior man easily dodges one problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoids' takes I out of EASILY, leaving EASLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Measly means contemptibly small or poor, a synonym of inferior or paltry.
